findings.title: Complex nested unit resolution logic with duplicated patterns
findings.description: The useEconomicData hook contains complex nested unit resolution logic (lines 61-77) that handles unit fallback in multiple places with similar patterns. The logic for determining unit priority (pointUnit -> group.unit -> defaultUnit) is repeated for both group-level and field-level, making it hard to maintain and prone to inconsistencies.
findings.suggested_issue: Extract unit resolution into a dedicated helper function like `resolveUnit(pointUnit, groupUnit, defaultUnit)` to eliminate duplication and centralize the fallback logic

findings.title: Duplicated item mapping logic across resolver methods
findings.description: The economic-data.resolver.ts file contains nearly identical item mapping code in three methods: getEconomicData (lines 34-41), economicDataFetchConfigs (lines 56-62), and updateEconomicDataFetchConfig (lines 87-93). Each method manually maps item properties with the same null-coalescing patterns.
findings.snippet:
item: {
  slug: point.item.slug,
  displayName: point.item.displayName,
  groupLabel: point.item.groupLabel ?? undefined,
  defaultUnit: point.item.defaultUnit ?? null,
  metadata: (point.item.metadata as Record<string, unknown> | null) ?? null
}
findings.suggested_issue: Create a shared `mapEconomicDataItem(item)` helper function to transform database item entities to GraphQL models consistently across all resolver methods

findings.title: Duplicated parser payload processing patterns
findings.description: The akshare.service.ts contains five parser methods (parseLatestPayload, parseTimeseriesPayload, parseMacroPayload, parseYearMonthPayload, parseYieldCurvePayload) that share nearly identical deduplication and field processing logic. Each method has its own Set for deduplication and similar flatMap patterns.
findings.suggested_issue: Create a generic parser base function that accepts a timestamp extractor and field configuration, then have specific parsers call this base with their unique extraction logic

findings.title: Magic numbers for threshold values without documentation
findings.description: The useEconomicData hook uses magic numbers for insight thresholds (20 for volatility, 5 for trend) without explaining their significance. Similarly, akshare.service.ts uses undocumented constants like 2_000_000 for batch max bytes and 1000 for batch size.
findings.suggested_issue: Extract magic numbers into named constants with JSDoc comments explaining the business rationale (e.g., VOLATILITY_THRESHOLD = 20 // Percentage deviation from average considered significant)

findings.title: Inconsistent naming between Chinese and English field labels
findings.description: The akshare.definitions.ts mixes Chinese field names (e.g., '开盘价', '收盘价') with English labels in some places, and the series.ts utility has to handle both conventions with fallback logic. This creates maintenance burden and potential for mismatches.
findings.snippet:
const openKey = resolveFieldKey(group, "open") ?? resolveFieldKey(group, "开盘价");
const closeKey = resolveFieldKey(group, "close") ?? resolveFieldKey(group, "收盘价");
findings.suggested_issue: Standardize on a single naming convention (preferably English for code) and use a translation layer or mapping object for display purposes. Add a FIELD_NAME_MAP constant to centralize the Chinese-English mappings

findings.title: Missing JSDoc documentation for public interfaces and hooks
findings.description: The useEconomicData hook and its exported interfaces (EconomicSeriesOptions, EconomicSeriesField, EconomicSeriesGroup, EconomicSeriesMap) lack JSDoc documentation explaining their purpose, parameters, and return values. This makes it harder for consumers to understand the API contract.
findings.suggested_issue: Add JSDoc comments to all exported interfaces and the main hook function describing: purpose, parameter meanings, return value structure, and usage examples

findings.title: Complex conditional chain in chartState derivation
findings.description: The chartState useMemo in useEconomicData.ts uses a sequential if-else chain that implicitly encodes state priority. The logic flow (error -> loading -> empty -> delayed -> ok) is not immediately obvious and could be clearer with explicit state machine or priority documentation.
findings.suggested_issue: Add a comment block explaining the state priority order, or refactor to use a state machine pattern with explicit priority constants for better maintainability

findings.title: Hardcoded fallback strings in insight generation
findings.description: The economic-chart-card.tsx has a hardcoded English fallback string (line 90) that bypasses the i18n system when translation keys are missing. This creates inconsistent user experience and makes the fallback logic fragile.
findings.suggested_issue: Use the i18n defaultValue parameter consistently instead of checking for missing keys, or ensure all translation keys are properly defined in the translation files

findings.title: Overly long service class with multiple responsibilities
findings.description: The AkshareService class (1202 lines) handles too many responsibilities: catalog management, job scheduling, HTTP requests, payload parsing, data persistence, and status tracking. This violates the Single Responsibility Principle and makes the class difficult to test and maintain.
findings.suggested_issue: Split AkshareService into focused services: AkshareCatalogService (catalog management), AkshareSchedulerService (job scheduling), AkshareParserService (payload parsing), AkshareDataService (data persistence)

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling patterns
findings.description: The akshare.service.ts uses different error handling patterns: some methods throw InternalServerErrorException, others log and return, and some have nested try-catch blocks. The formatError method truncates errors to 191 characters without explanation.
findings.suggested_issue: Standardize error handling with a consistent pattern (e.g., always throw typed exceptions for recoverable errors, always log for non-recoverable). Document the 191 character limit (likely a database column constraint)

findings.title: Type assertion without validation in tooltip formatter
findings.description: The buildOption function in economic-chart-card.tsx uses 'any' type for tooltip formatter params without proper type guards, which could lead to runtime errors if the ECharts API changes.
findings.suggested_issue: Define a proper TypeScript interface for ECharts tooltip params or use the official ECharts types, and add runtime validation for the expected structure

findings.title: Redundant null checks after array access
findings.description: The series.ts utility has redundant null checks after array access patterns that TypeScript's strict mode should handle. For example, checking if values[values.length - 1] is truthy after already checking values.length > 0.
findings.suggested_issue: Use TypeScript's non-null assertion operator or array.at(-1) method with proper typing to reduce redundant checks while maintaining type safety

findings.title: Hardcoded color values instead of theme tokens
findings.description: The market-pulse.tsx component uses hardcoded color values like '#13c2c2' (cyan) alongside theme colors, creating inconsistency. The MetricValue component also uses hardcoded Tailwind classes for flash effects instead of theme variables.
findings.suggested_issue: Define all colors in the chart theme configuration and reference them consistently. Replace hardcoded hex values with theme.colors.* references

findings.title: Missing description field in multiple data definitions
findings.description: Several AkshareDataItemDefinition entries in akshare.definitions.ts are missing the optional 'description' field, which would help users understand what each data item represents. Only some entries like 'gold-futures-realtime' have descriptions.
findings.suggested_issue: Add description fields to all data item definitions to improve discoverability and provide context for dashboard users

findings.title: Inconsistent variable naming for override logic
findings.description: The ensureCatalog method uses poorly named variables 'mergedMetadataWithOverrides' and 'mergedMetadataWithOverrides2' for sequential override applications, making the code harder to follow.
findings.suggested_issue: Rename to descriptive names like 'metadataWithParserOverride' and 'metadataWithAllOverrides', or refactor to use a single reduce/pipeline pattern for applying overrides
